q: A measure μ on a topological space X is called regular if:
opts: μ is inner regular (μ(A) = sup{μ(K) : K⊆A, K compact}) and outer regular (μ(A) = inf{μ(U) : U⊇A, U open})
μ is absolutely continuous w.r.t. Lebesgue measure
exp: Regularity means Borel sets can be approximated from inside by compact sets and from outside by open sets. Radon measures (locally finite regular Borel measures) are the natural class for analysis on locally compact spaces.
